subject: Non-deterministic token truncation during streaming — triage & hotfix plan
summary: Customer observed intermittent truncation of streaming responses during a live pilot demo. Sales engaged Platform/Runtime for triage. Short-term mitigation (disable continuous batching for tenant) applied and validated; long-term fix scheduled in next runtime release. Mutual action plan laid out for customer communication and follow-up patch.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Non-deterministic token truncation observed during StratusAI pilot — immediate triage requested

Karthik / Dev / Rishi,

Quick summary: During a pilot demo with StratusAI this morning (10:45 PT), the customer saw streaming outputs cut off mid-sentence in ~3/20 sessions. The payloads were short (prompt + max_tokens: 40) and streaming=true. The issue is non-deterministic — same prompt sometimes returns full completion, sometimes truncates at token boundary. Customer-facing demo was impacted; execs were on the call.

Repro steps (from Stratus):
- Model: rdx-gptx-8b (hosted)
- Endpoint: /v1/generate?stream=true
- Body: {"prompt": "<short instruction>", "max_tokens": 40, "temperature": 0.2}
- Observed: final token stream ends with partial word, connection remains open for ~200ms then ends.

Attached: heap-trace.txt (their capture), stratus-sample-request.json (sanitized).

Immediate asks:
1) Can Runtime confirm whether this looks like a streaming flush / chunking bug vs. model-side truncation?
2) If runtime-side, can we apply a tenant-scoped mitigation before Stratus' next demo at 16:00 PT today?
3) ETA on root-cause and customer-facing statement we can share by EOD.

Severity is effectively P1 for this account (pilot -> expansion). Evelyn, I added you in case we need CS involvement for the exec follow-up.

Thanks — please flag if you need anything else from Stratus (they can provision full server logs on request).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Non-deterministic token truncation observed during StratusAI pilot — immediate triage requested

Thanks for the clear repro, Marissa. I dug into runtime logs for the tenant and saw matching request IDs for the times you listed. Initial observations:

- The model itself returns full logits sequences upstream (we've confirmed with a debug capture to the model host).
- Truncation correlates with batch flush events where continuous batching combines multiple inflight requests and then performs a KV-cache rotation/eviction when sequence boundaries are reached.
- In several traces, the stream boundary handler appears to emit the final chunk before the full finishing token buffer is populated (race in flush -> close path).

Short-term mitigations we can apply tenant-scoped (low risk):
- Disable continuous batching for StratusAI tenant on the serving pool (config toggle). This prevents combined flush/race conditions. Latency will increase slightly (p50 +12ms), cost impact minimal for short requests.
- Alternative: pin the tenant to model-variant rdx-gptx-8b-stable (older variant without the new batching combinator) — also feasible if you prefer no runtime config changes.

I need access to the full raw server logs (token-level traces) for two failing request IDs to confirm the exact flush ordering — asking Stratus to paste those into heap-trace (they said they can). If you want an immediate customer-facing mitigation, I can disable batching for the tenant now and test with their sample.

Attached: quick-rollback-commands.txt (inline below) — note this is a config toggle, reversible.

Command (ops):
> infra runtime-config set tenant.stratusai.continuous_batching false --env=prod --apply-now

If you want me to run this, call it out and I’ll coordinate with On-Call to apply and smoke-test.

—Dev
Dev Patel | Senior SRE, Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Non-deterministic token truncation observed during StratusAI pilot — immediate triage requested

Appreciate the triage, Dev. Two quick product/field questions before we pull the trigger:

1) If we disable continuous batching for StratusAI, what's the expected customer-visible impact? You mentioned ~+12ms p50 — any effect on throughput for their current pilot traffic (very bursty)?
2) Who is the owner to roll this change and verify the fix in prod (I want a single point of contact to tell Stratus)?

Proposed mutual action plan (for Execs):
- Plan A (fast): Disable continuous batching for tenant by 12:30 PT, run 10 quick streaming checks with Stratus sample payload, validate no truncation.
- Plan B (fallback): If Plan A insufficient, switch tenant to rdx-gptx-8b-stable by 13:00 PT and re-run validation.
- Communication: Marissa to send customer note confirming we applied a config change and will follow up with full RCA by EOD.

Can you confirm you can do Plan A now and own verification? If yes I’ll tell Stratus we have an ops owner and ETA. Attaching a mutual-action-plan PDF for the exec channel.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Non-deterministic token truncation observed during StratusAI pilot — triage & hotfix plan

Update / resolution: we executed Plan A at 14:12 PT (disabled continuous batching for tenant.stratusai on prod). Steps performed: 
- infra runtime-config set tenant.stratusai.continuous_batching false --env=prod --apply-now
- Ran a 10-request streaming suite using the stratus sample; 0/10 truncated.
- Customer validated on their side during the 14:30 demo (they confirmed full sentences now).

Root cause (short): a race in the batching combinator where an early flush on batch boundary triggered stream-close before the final token buffer drain completed when KV-cache eviction overlapped the flush. We have an identified patch (change batching-combinator flush ordering + guard) and have scheduled it for release 1.12.3 (ETA: 2026-09-22).

Impact and next steps: 
- Short-term: change is tenant-scoped and reversible. Latency impact negligible for Stratus pilot traffic profile.
- Long-term: patch will fix the combinator ordering and include additional regression tests for streaming token correctness.
- Action items: Marissa to send customer-facing note (I can provide two-sentence technical blurb). Karthik to update deal notes with mitigation performed. I’ll attach the patch reference in JIRA SUP-9821 and ping QA for the release.

Commands applied (ops audit):
- runtime-config: {tenant: stratusai, continuous_batching: false, applied_by: rishi_malhotra, applied_at: 2026-09-14T14:12:00-07:00}

Let me know if you want us to proactively roll the stable model-variant for additional safety — not strictly necessary now.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Principal Runtime Engineer
